target.title: fix(gateway): preserve abort after dispatch rejection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #90999.

Users can see contradictory or missing terminal state when `chat.send` dispatch fails around abort/session-lifecycle timing. The bad windows are:

- abort already won, but a later post-dispatch rejection can overwrite the cached terminal result as an error;
- dispatch already failed, but a late `chat.abort` during fallback persistence can mask the real error as an abort;
- a queued followup was accepted, then an explicit abort won before dispatch rejection, and the accepted-followup branch could otherwise bypass the abort-preserve dedupe write;
- session lifecycle interruption after `chat.send` ACK can abort the controller without going through the normal `chat.abort` marker/broadcast path, leaving the client without a terminal `chat` event or keeping the session admission busy after terminal abort.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict refresh keeps current `main` session-admission, queued-followup, and dispatch-error lifecycle behavior, then makes terminal ownership explicit:

- if `chat.abort` already recorded the abort marker, preserve the abort terminal result, write the aborted dedupe, release session admission/active-run ownership before fallback persistence, and do not resurrect the run as an error;
- if a followup was already queued and no explicit abort marker owns the run, keep that accepted client run terminal;
- if dispatch/error owns the terminal state, close abortability before any awaited fallback persistence, clear stale abort state, cache the error, and broadcast the error;
- if lifecycle admission interrupts the run, do not treat a bare aborted signal as proof that a terminal abort was already broadcast.

The PR remains limited to `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts` and `src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts`.

## User Impact

`chat.send` clients now receive one stable terminal outcome for these race windows. Same-run retries observe the correct cached terminal result, late abort does not rewrite a real dispatch error, lifecycle-interrupted sends still produce a terminal `chat` event, queued followup admission still terminalizes the accepted client run unless an explicit abort owns the run, and lifecycle operations are not held behind unrelated fallback transcript persistence after a terminal abort.

Related: #84176 and #84306.

## Evidence

Candidate head / proof head: `5c2e32c3728d025942fd4d0828a65b15a5f5cf8f`

Green upstream base merged for this branch refresh: `8df18050d53298a6fc94740fbc06978719b5e916` (`openclaw/openclaw` `main`, CI run `28737444248` succeeded). The merge-tree against that base is clean, and the PR-style diff remains exactly the two Gateway files listed above.

Commands run on the current proof head:

```shell
node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts -t "queued followup rejection after abort"
node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts -t "post-dispatch rejection after abort"
node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts -t "post-dispatch rejection stays error when abort arrives during error persistence"
node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts -t "lifecycle-interrupted dispatch rejection"
node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts -t "terminalizes the client run when a followup is queued"
node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts
node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat.test.ts
git diff --check 8df18050d53298a6fc94740fbc06978719b5e916...HEAD
git merge-tree --write-tree 8df18050d53298a6fc94740fbc06978719b5e916 HEAD
```

Observed result:

```text
queued followup rejection after abort: 1 test passed, 55 skipped
post-dispatch rejection after abort: 1 test passed, 55 skipped
post-dispatch rejection stays error when abort arrives during error persistence: 1 test passed, 55 skipped
lifecycle-interrupted dispatch rejection: 1 test passed, 55 skipped
terminalizes the client run when a followup is queued: 1 test passed, 55 skipped
server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts: 56 tests passed
server.chat.gateway-server-chat.test.ts: 38 tests passed
git diff --check: no output
merge-tree: clean (`6fd6c005299a0ebb6d2c0d5afbcc9fdd2416f1e8`)
```

Real Gateway / WebSocket proof was also run on the same proof head with a real OpenClaw Gateway server and real WebSocket RPC client calls (`chat.send` / `chat.abort`). The only controlled boundary is dispatch, using the repository's normal Gateway test seam, so the proof exercises the Gateway server, WebSocket transport, RPC request/response shape, and client-visible `chat` broadcasts without claiming a live provider/model E2E run.

```shell
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/pr91000-websocket-proof.test.ts
```

Observed result:

```text
gateway-core: 2 tests passed
gateway-server: 2 tests passed
gateway-client: 2 tests passed
overall: 3 test files passed, 6 tests passed
```

WebSocket proof output summary:

```json
{
  "proofKind": "real Gateway server + WebSocket RPC harness with controlled dispatch boundary",
  "branchHead": "5c2e32c3728d025942fd4d0828a65b15a5f5cf8f",
  "abortFirst": {
    "chat.send": { "ok": true, "payload": { "runId": "ws-proof-abort-first", "status": "started" } },
    "chat.abort": { "ok": true, "payload": { "ok": true, "aborted": true, "runIds": ["ws-proof-abort-first"] } },
    "dispatchSawAbortedSignal": true,
    "chatBroadcastStates": ["aborted"]
  },
  "errorFirstLateAbort": {
    "chat.send": { "ok": true, "payload": { "runId": "ws-proof-error-first", "status": "started" } },
    "chat.abort": { "ok": true, "payload": { "ok": true, "aborted": false, "runIds": [] } },
    "retryDuringPending": { "ok": false, "payload": { "runId": "ws-proof-error-first", "status": "error", "summary": "Error: dispatch failed before late abort" }, "error": { "code": "UNAVAILABLE" } },
    "midWindowChatBroadcastStates": [],
    "chatBroadcastStates": ["error"]
  }
}
```

Regression coverage now includes:

- abort-first post-dispatch rejection preserves the terminal timeout/aborted result, serves that cached result to same-run retry, emits no error chat state, and releases lifecycle admission before pending runtime transcript persistence settles;
- queued-followup plus explicit abort still preserves the terminal abort, does not emit a final/error chat state after dispatch rejection, and serves the cached aborted result to same-run retry;
- error-first post-dispatch rejection closes abortability before fallback persistence, makes late `chat.abort` return `aborted:false`, serves cached error during the pending window, emits no aborted chat state, and allows a later retry after error dedupe cleanup;
- lifecycle admission interruption after dispatch start still emits a terminal `chat` error event when no `chat.abort` marker/broadcast exists;
- queued followup admission still terminalizes the accepted client run and keeps the queued turn cached until the followup completes;
- the sibling dispatch-error/session lifecycle suite still passes.

Current branch-refresh note: upstream `main` CI recovered at `8df18050d53298a6fc94740fbc06978719b5e916`, so this branch was merged with that green base to trigger a fresh PR check run. The prior `check-lint` and `check-docs` failures reported files outside this PR diff (`src/crestodian/onboarding-welcome.ts`, `docs/start/onboarding-overview.md`, and `docs/start/onboarding.md`); this PR still changes only the two Gateway files listed above.

Local touched-file oxlint was attempted in this linked checkout, but the shared `node_modules` has oxlint `1.67.0` while current `main` requires `1.72.0`; oxlint exits while parsing the refreshed config before reading source (`unicorn/no-array-fill-with-reference-type` is unknown to the installed binary). No dependency install was run in this linked checkout.

What was not tested: browser UI, native clients, and live provider/model E2E were not run.
